items.title: Bobby Hutcherson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He made this offer to all the people who were – Hubert Laws, everybody – to pay everybody $1,000 to do a record.

ctx.x: . . . Columbia. He made this offer to all the people who were – Hubert Laws, everybody – to pay everybody $1,000 to do a record. Then he would try to make it up. He was taking money out of the producing – the budget – and putting it in his pocket. Sorry. They caught up with him. He wrote down – I came over to his office one time, and he had a brown paper bag lunch, and he wrote down this contract on a brown paper sack. I went for it. So did all those great musicians who were with Blue Note at that time. He made…
There’s all these camels, man, and they’re waiting for the light to turn green. Ain’t nobody out there but – that’s some funny stuff. I saw that and . . .

items.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I do remember a session we did with him up in San Francisco

ctx.x: . . Bobby Hutcherson, yeah. We just interviewed him back in December. He talked about L.A. back in the late ’50s, early ’60s, and the scene. He really gave us a sense of what L.A. was like for him coming up.
